findings.scenario: Identity scan covers only requiredArtifacts via a short blockedTerms list, then fs.cp copies the whole tree (extra files, logs, nested dirs, symlinks). Path B source/provider text such as 'Refero', 'refero.design', 'Path A', model names, timing, or cost is required by the rubric's Source credibility / Efficiency evidence and is not in blockedTerms ('refero mcp', 'path-a', …). A symlink whose basename is not provenance.json is copied un-audited. Evaluator-facing presentation can therefore reveal producer identity while assemble-blind still succeeds.
findings.remediation: Copy only regular files from the required non-provenance list after realpath-confining them under the path artifact dir. Reject symlinks. Scan every copied byte for path labels, provider/model tokens (including 'refero' and URL hosts), and timing/cost fields; require neutral source IDs in presentation files.

findings.scenario: unblind only calls validateCompletedArtifacts plus validateHumanScores. It does not require assemble-blind, a presentation packet, or a passed leak check. A coordinator can score labeled artifacts/path-a and artifacts/path-b, supply any non-empty attestation, and obtain UNBLINDED_HUMAN_SCORES_RECORDED. Blinding is a documented convention, not a gate.
findings.remediation: Make unblind depend on an existing packet whose contents re-pass the leak scan; bind scores.runManifestSha256 and a packet/presentation hash; refuse unblind if presentation is missing or stale.

findings.scenario: unblind overwrites unblinded-results.json on every success. After the mapping is known, scores can be edited and unblind re-run, replacing the human-score record. The human-score gate is not a one-way freeze.
findings.remediation: If unblinded-results.json exists, refuse unless the new record's scoreSha256 and bytes are identical. Write via temp file + atomic rename.

findings.scenario: Provenance is 'complete' if required keys exist, status is completed, runManifestSha256 matches, and list fields are arrays. prompts/models/sources/outputHashes may all be []. outputHashes are never checked against artifact bytes. Dummy files plus empty provenance flip the run from honest BLOCKED into assemble-blind/unblind success and look like live results.
findings.remediation: For status=completed require non-empty prompts and models, meteredCalls present (empty only when claimed), and outputHashes covering every required artifact with matching sha256. Treat empty or mismatched provenance as BLOCKED.

findings.scenario: Frozen rubric requires two evaluators with randomized A/B labels. humanGate and validateHumanScores accept a single named evaluator and one scores file, then unblind. Inter-rater disagreement (called out in comparison-status.md) cannot be enforced.
findings.remediation: Require two independent score files with distinct evaluator names, both bound to the same manifest/packet hash, before writing unblinded results.

findings.scenario: The hashed brief freezes site, DESIGN.md, business-intelligence.json, token-inventory.json, etc. The evaluation contract/harness freeze a different set (research.json, design-contract.md, token-proposal.json, site-manifest.json, provenance.json). Identical-input / output-artifact constancy is two conflicting truths; a path can pass the harness while missing the brief's artifacts (or the reverse).
findings.remediation: Version a single required-artifact list in the contract that is a superset of the brief, or make verifyContract fail if brief.requiredArtifacts is not exactly the non-provenance contract set.

findings.scenario: Existence check uses fs.access and swallows every error except the synthetic 'run already exists' message (including EACCES). Manifest and unblinding.json are written non-atomically. A half-created run directory permanently blocks retry; a lost race or swallowed error can overwrite an 'immutable' run and break the unblinding binding.
findings.remediation: Treat EEXIST/existing run-manifest.json as immutable; rethrow other access errors; write manifest+unblinding in a temp directory and rename into place only when both files are complete.

findings.scenario: run-manifest.json stores the seed and algorithm. Path IDs are public in the frozen contract, so seededOrder(seed, ['path-a','path-b']) reconstructs the mapping without unblinding.json. Anyone given the run directory (not only presentation/) is unblinded.
findings.remediation: Keep seed and mapping only in coordinator-only unblinding.json; store a seed hash (not the seed) in the manifest; document that evaluators must receive a copied presentation/ tree with no sibling run files.

findings.line: completed provenance plus full human scores test ~91-128
findings.scenario: Tests never assert mapped pathId order, never call unblind/assemble-blind on a BLOCKED run, and writeCompletedArtifacts uses empty outputHashes. A swapped mapping or a dropped BLOCKED gate still passes.
findings.remediation: Assert exact pathId↔blindId mapping for the fixed seed, assert unblind/assemble-blind throw on BLOCKED fixtures, and require hashed outputHashes in the completed-artifact helper.

audit.proof_assessment: No external proof artifacts were supplied. In-repo node:test cases only show happy-path verify/prepare/unblind and one blocked-term leak; they do not independently recompute lock/input hashes here and are too weak to certify blinding, provenance completeness, or immutability. Deterministic tests were treated as claims, not authority.
residual_risks: Live-runner honesty (identical prompts/builder, no hidden paid fallback) is not mechanically attested beyond self-reported provenance.
Operational leakage if evaluators receive the whole run directory rather than a copied presentation/ packet.
SHA-256 lock and input digests were not recomputed in this review; a lock/input mismatch would only surface when verifyContract is actually executed.
Efficiency scoring needs time/cost that the blinding contract forbids in presentation files, so honest blind Efficiency scores remain underspecified even after leak-scan hardening.
